title_en: Regulations on the Sharing of Government Data

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China, the Data Security Law of the People's Republic of China, the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, and other laws, for the purposes of promoting safe, orderly, and efficient sharing and utilization of government data, enhancing the government's digital governance capacity and administrative service efficiency, and comprehensively building a digital government.

Article 2 These Regulations apply to the sharing of government data among government departments and organizations authorized by laws and regulations to perform public administration functions (hereinafter collectively referred to as government departments), as well as related security, supervision, management, and other work.

Article 3 For the purposes of these Regulations, "government data" means all types of data collected and generated by government departments in the course of performing their duties according to law, excluding data that constitutes State secrets or work secrets.
For the purposes of these Regulations, "government data sharing" means the act of a government department, due to the need to perform its duties according to law, using government data of other government departments or providing government data to other government departments.

Article 4 The work of government data sharing shall adhere to the leadership of the Communist Party of China, implement a holistic approach to national security, coordinate development and security, and follow the principles of overall coordination, unified standards, lawful sharing, reasonable use, and security and controllability.

Article 5 In conducting government data sharing, government departments shall comply with laws and regulations, fulfill government data security protection obligations, and shall not harm national security or public interests, nor infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, or other organizations.
Article 6 The State shall establish a government data sharing standards system to promote the standardization and normalization of government data sharing work.

Article 7 The State encourages management innovation, mechanism innovation, and technological innovation in the field of government data sharing, and continuously improves the efficiency, application level, and security assurance capability of government data sharing.

Article 8 People's governments at all levels shall strengthen the organizational leadership of government data sharing work.
The competent department of government data sharing under the State Council shall be responsible for coordinating and promoting government data sharing work nationwide.
The competent department of government data sharing under the local people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for coordinating and promoting government data sharing work within its administrative region.
All departments of the State Council shall be responsible for government data sharing work within their respective departments, and shall coordinate and guide government data sharing work in their respective industries and fields.

Article 9 The competent department of government data sharing shall, together with other government departments, study major matters and important work in government data sharing, summarize and promote typical cases and experiences of government data sharing, and coordinate the promotion of safe, orderly, and efficient sharing and utilization of government data across levels, regions, systems, departments, and businesses.

Article 10 Government departments shall fulfill their primary responsibilities for government data sharing, establish and improve the government data sharing work system of their own departments, and organize the study and resolution of major issues in government data sharing.

Article 12 Government data shall be subject to unified catalog management. The competent department of government data sharing under the State Council shall formulate the standards and specifications for compiling government data catalogs, and organize the compilation of the national government data catalog. The competent department of government data sharing under the local people's government at or above the county level shall organize the compilation of the government data catalog within its administrative region.
Government departments shall, in accordance with their own responsibilities and the standards and specifications for compiling government data catalogs, compile the government data catalog of their own departments.

Article 13 When compiling government data catalogs, government departments shall, according to law, conduct assessments of confidentiality risks, personal information protection impacts, etc., and obtain the review and approval of the department head.
The government data catalog shall specify information such as the catalog name, data items, providing entity, data format, data update frequency, sharing attributes, sharing methods, use conditions, and data classification and grading.

Article 15 Government departments shall scientifically and reasonably determine the sharing attributes of government data, and shall not obstruct or affect government data sharing by, among other means, arbitrarily adding conditions.
For government data belonging to the conditional sharing category, government departments shall specify in the government data catalog the sharing scope, intended use, and other conditions for sharing and use. For government data belonging to the no-sharing category, government departments shall specify in the government data catalog the reasons and clarify the corresponding basis in laws, administrative regulations, and decisions of the State Council.

Article 16 Government departments shall submit the compiled government data catalogs to the competent department of government data sharing at the same level for review. After the review is passed, the competent department of government data sharing shall uniformly notify the government departments.
Government departments shall, by reference to the uniformly released government data catalogs, enrich government data resources, ensure government data quality, and share government data according to law.

Article 17 Government data catalogs shall be subject to dynamic updating.
Where a government data catalog needs corresponding updating due to adjustments to laws, administrative regulations, or decisions of the State Council, or changes in the responsibilities of a government department, the government department shall complete the update to the government data catalog within 10 working days from the date of such adjustment or change, and submit it to the competent department of government data sharing at the same level for review. If the update period needs to be extended due to special reasons, it may be extended by 5 working days with the consent of the competent department of government data sharing at the same level.
The competent department of government data sharing shall complete the review and release within 2 working days from the date of receiving the updated government data catalog.

Article 18 Government departments shall establish and improve a whole-process quality management system for government data, improve the capability of government data quality management, and strengthen standardized management of government data collection, storage, processing, transmission, sharing, use, and destruction.

Article 19 Government departments shall collect government data in accordance with statutory functions, powers, procedures, and standards. If government data obtained through sharing can satisfy the needs for performing duties, government departments shall not repeatedly collect such data from citizens, legal persons, or other organizations.
Where the collection of government data involves multiple government departments, the competent department of government data sharing shall designate the government department responsible for leading the collection as the data source department. The data source department shall strengthen coordination and information exchange with other relevant government departments, promptly improve and update government data, ensure the integrity, accuracy, and usability of government data, and uniformly provide government data sharing services.

Article 20 The competent department of government data sharing shall establish a supply-demand matching mechanism for government data sharing and clarify the work procedures.
The government data demand department shall, based on the needs of performing its duties and in accordance with the uniformly released government data catalog, and with the consent of the head of its government data sharing working body, submit a government data sharing application according to law, specifying the basis for use, usage scenario, scope of use, sharing method, usage period, etc., and guarantee the authenticity, legality, and necessity of the government data sharing application.
The government data provider department shall, within the time limit specified in Article 21 of these Regulations, review the government data sharing application submitted by the government data demand department, and after obtaining the consent of the head of its government data sharing working body, issue a reply.

Article 21 Where the government data applied for sharing by the government data demand department falls into the unconditional sharing category, the government data provider department shall issue a reply within 1 working day from the date of receipt of the government data sharing application; if it falls into the conditional sharing category, it shall issue a reply within 10 working days from the date of receipt of the application indicating whether it agrees to the sharing. If the reply period needs to be extended due to special reasons, the government data provider department shall report to and obtain the consent of the competent department of government data sharing at the same level, and notify the government data demand department; the extended period shall not exceed 10 working days at most.
If the application materials submitted by the government data demand department are incomplete, the government data provider department shall inform it at one time of the materials to be supplemented, and shall not directly refuse the application. If the government data provider department does not agree to the sharing, it shall state the reasons.

Article 22 The government data provider department shall share the government data within 20 working days from the date of making the reply agreeing to the sharing.
The government data provider department may share the government data with the government data demand department through methods such as service interfaces, batch exchange, or file download.

Article 23 The State encourages government departments at all levels to optimize the review process for government data sharing and shorten the time for review and provision of shared government data.

Article 24 The higher-level government department shall, based on the needs of the lower-level government department in performing its duties, and on the premise of ensuring the security of government data, promptly and completely return the government data collected and generated by the business information system within the administrative region of the lower-level government, and shall properly conduct system integration and business coordination, and shall not impose additional restrictive conditions.
After obtaining the returned government data, the lower-level government department shall share and use it according to the needs of performing its duties, and shall ensure the security of the relevant government data.

Article 25 Where government departments obtain government data through sharing, they shall not arbitrarily expand the scope of use or use it for or in disguised form for other purposes, and shall not arbitrarily provide the obtained government data to any third party. If it is truly necessary to expand the scope of use, use it for other purposes, or provide it to a third party, the consent of the government data provider department shall be obtained.
The competent department of government data sharing and other government departments shall take measures to prevent the risk of leakage caused by the aggregation and linkage of government data.

Article 26 The competent department of government data sharing under the State Council shall coordinate the establishment of a government data verification and correction system.
Government departments shall, in accordance with their own responsibilities, establish rules for government data verification and correction and provide channels for correction. The government data demand department shall record the usage status of government data, and if it discovers that the government data is inaccurate or incomplete, it shall promptly submit a government data verification request to the government data provider department. The government data provider department shall, within 10 working days from the date of receipt of the government data verification request, verify, correct, and provide feedback on the verification result.

Article 27 Where the purpose of sharing government data obtained by the government data demand department through sharing has been achieved, cannot be achieved, or is no longer necessary for achieving the sharing purpose, it shall be properly disposed of in accordance with the requirements of the government data provider department.
If a government data demand department arbitrarily exceeds the scope of use or uses the government data for purposes beyond the sharing purpose, or arbitrarily provides the government data to a third party, the competent department of government data sharing or the government data provider department shall suspend its authority to share government data and urge it to rectify within a specified period; if it refuses to rectify or fails to rectify adequately, the sharing may be terminated.
The government data provider department shall not, without proper justification, terminate or alter the government data sharing services already provided. If it is truly necessary to terminate or alter the services, the government data provider department shall consult with the government data demand department and report to the competent department of government data sharing at the same level for recordation.

Article 28 The competent department of government data sharing shall establish and improve a dispute resolution mechanism for government data sharing.
Where a dispute on government data sharing arises between a government data demand department and a government data provider department at the same level, they shall resolve it through consultation; if consultation fails, they shall apply to the competent department of government data sharing at the same level for coordination and handling in accordance with the procedures. Where a dispute on government data sharing arises across levels or regions, it shall be coordinated and handled by the common competent department of government data sharing at the higher level. If no agreement is reached after coordination and handling by the competent department of government data sharing, it shall be submitted to the people's government at the same level as that competent department for decision.

Article 29 The competent department of government data sharing shall supervise and inspect the status of government data sharing, and may give notice of acts that violate the provisions of these Regulations.
The government data demand department shall record the usage scenario, usage process, application results, storage status, destruction status, etc., of the shared government data, and the retention period of relevant records shall be no less than 3 years. The competent department of government data sharing and the government data provider department may inspect the relevant records of the government data demand department. If otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 30 The State shall coordinate the construction of data infrastructure, improve the security protection capability of government data, and integrate and build a national integrated government big data system that is unified in standards, reasonable in layout, coordinated in management, and safe and reliable.
The competent department of government data sharing under the State Council shall coordinate the construction and management of the national integrated government big data system, and be responsible for integrating and building the national government big data platform, achieving interconnection and intercommunication with government data platforms of relevant departments of the State Council and government data platforms of various regions, and providing platform support for government data sharing.
The competent department of government data sharing under the local people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for the construction and management of the government data platform within its administrative region, and share government data with townships (sub-districts) and villages (communities) as needed.
The relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for building and optimizing their own government data platforms, and may support government data sharing work in their respective industries and fields. If no government data platform has been built, they may conduct their department's government data sharing work through the national government big data platform.

Article 31 The government data platforms already built by government departments shall be incorporated into the national integrated government big data system. Unless otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations, in principle, government data sharing work across levels, regions, systems, departments, and businesses shall not be conducted by newly building government data sharing exchange systems.
Article 32 Government departments shall conduct relevant work on government data sharing through the national integrated government big data system.
Article 33 The State encourages and supports the application of new technologies such as big data, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and blockchain in government data sharing.

Article 34 The competent department of government data sharing shall, together with the departments of cyberspace administration, public security, state security, secrecy administration, and cryptography administration at the same level, in accordance with the data classification and grading protection system, promote the construction of the government data sharing security management system, clarify the responsible entities for security at each stage of government data sharing in accordance with the principle that those who manage are responsible and those who use are responsible, and supervise the implementation of government data sharing security management responsibilities.
If, during the use of government data shared according to law, the government data demand department experiences such situations as tampering, destruction, leakage, or illegal use of government data, it shall bear the security management responsibility.

Article 35 Government departments shall establish and improve a government data sharing security management system, fulfill their primary responsibilities for government data sharing security management and the requirements for classified and graded management of government data, and ensure the security of government data sharing.
Government departments shall adopt technical measures and other necessary measures to prevent government data from being tampered with, destroyed, leaked, or illegally obtained or used.
Government departments shall strengthen the monitoring of government data security risks, and when a government data security incident occurs, shall immediately initiate an emergency plan, take corresponding emergency response measures to prevent the expansion of harm and eliminate security risks, and report to the relevant competent departments in accordance with regulations.

Article 36 Where a government department entrusts another person to participate in the construction, operation, or maintenance of government informatization projects, or to store or process government data, it shall follow the approval procedures in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, clarify work norms and standards, adopt necessary technical measures, and supervise the entrusted party in fulfilling the corresponding government data security protection obligations. The entrusted party shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and the contract, fulfill its government data security protection obligations, and shall not arbitrarily access, obtain, retain, use, disclose, or provide government data to others.
The entity responsible for the construction and management of the government data platform shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and the mandatory requirements of national standards, ensure the safe and stable operation of the platform and safeguard the security of government data.

Article 37 When conducting government data sharing activities involving personal information, government departments and their staff shall comply with the provisions of the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulations on the Security Management of Network Data, and other laws and administrative regulations.
Citizens, legal persons, and other organizations have the right to complain or report acts that infringe upon their lawful rights and interests during the process of government data sharing. The government department receiving such complaints or reports shall handle them promptly in accordance with regulations.

Article 38 People's governments at or above the county level shall include the funds needed for government data sharing work in their respective budgets. People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall implement whole-process budget performance management for funds related to government data sharing. The status of government data sharing shall serve as an important basis for determining the investment in government informatization project construction, operation and maintenance funds, and the results of post-project evaluation.
The competent department of government data sharing shall strengthen supervision over the timeliness and data quality of data sharing by government data provider departments within its administrative region, as well as the data application situation and security assurance measures of government data demand departments, and shall report to the people's government at the same level.

Article 42 Where government departments or their staff disclose, sell, or illegally provide to others personal privacy, personal information, trade secrets, or confidential business information learned during the process of government data sharing, or are derelict of duty, abuse their power, or engage in malpractice for personal gain in government data sharing work, they shall be given sanctions according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 43 The State promotes data sharing between government departments and other State organs by reference to the provisions of these Regulations based on their respective needs for performing duties.
Article 44 These Regulations shall come into force as of August 1, 2025.
